claim: Sarcopenia is defined as the age-related degeneration of skeletal muscle mass and is characterized by a progressive decline in strength and performance.
source: Sarcopenia is defined as the age-related degeneration of skeletal muscle mass and is characterized by a progressive decline in strength and performance (Santilli et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Santilli et al., 2014

claim: Sarcopenia afflicts 5–13% of people aged 60–70 years.
source: This syndrome is prevalent in older adults and has been estimated by large scale studies to afflict 5–13% of people aged 60–70 years and expands to 50% of those aged 80 and above (von Haehling et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to von Haehling et al., 2010

claim: Sarcopenia expands to 50% of those aged 80 and above.
source: This syndrome is prevalent in older adults and has been estimated by large scale studies to afflict 5–13% of people aged 60–70 years and expands to 50% of those aged 80 and above (von Haehling et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to von Haehling et al., 2010

claim: Loss of muscle function is associated with a decline in quality of life and higher mortality and morbidity rates due to increased chance of falls and fractures.
source: Loss of muscle function is associated with a decline in quality of life and higher mortality and morbidity rates due to increased chance of falls and fractures (Tsekoura et al., 2017; Ahmadpanah et al., 2015 ).
evidence: Supported by citations to Tsekoura et al., 2017 and Ahmadpanah et al., 2015

claim: Sarcopenia is linked to risk factors, such as a sedentary lifestyle, lack of exercise, and a diet deficient in protein and micronutrients.
source: Sarcopenia is linked to risk factors, such as a sedentary lifestyle, lack of exercise, and a diet deficient in protein and micronutrients (Tsekoura et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tsekoura et al., 2017

claim: Several aspects of the molecular basis of the age-dependent decline in muscle health remain unknown.

evidence: Statement of current knowledge gap in the field

claim: Age-related muscle function is clearly linked to frailty.
source: Although age-related muscle function is clearly linked to frailty (Dent et al., 2019), previously, different etiologies of clinical weakness led to discrepancies in the definitions of sarcopenia (Batsis et al., 2013; Cruz-Jentoft et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dent et al., 2019

claim: Different etiologies of clinical weakness led to discrepancies in the definitions of sarcopenia.

claim: The prevalence of sarcopenia begins in the fourth decade of life.

source: The US Health and Retirement Study (HRS) is a nationally representative survey of adults aged 50 years and older and has proven to be an invaluable dataset for investigating the normal aging processes (Fisher and Ryan, 2018; Sonnega et al., 2014; Juster and Suzman, 1995; HRS Health and Retirement Study, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Fisher and Ryan, 2018; Sonnega et al., 2014; Juster and Suzman, 1995; HRS Health and Retirement Study, 2021

claim: The HRS has proven to be an invaluable dataset for investigating the normal aging processes.
source: The US Health and Retirement Study (HRS) is a nationally representative survey of adults aged 50 years and older and has proven to be an invaluable dataset for investigating the normal aging processes (Fisher and Ryan, 2018; Sonnega et al., 2014; Juster and Suzman, 1995; HRS Health and Retirement Study, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Fisher and Ryan, 2018; Sonnega et al., 2014; Juster and Suzman, 1995; HRS Health and Retirement Study, 2021

claim: In Caenorhabditis elegans, alh-6 is 88% identical to ALDH4A1 in humans.
source: In Caenorhabditis elegans, mutation of the conserved proline catabolic gene alh-6 (88% identity to ALDH4A1 in humans) leads to premature aging and impaired muscle mitochondrial function (Pang and Curran, 2014).
evidence: Stated as a fact with citation to Pang and Curran, 2014

claim: Mutation of alh-6 in C. elegans leads to premature aging and impaired muscle mitochondrial function.
source: In Caenorhabditis elegans, mutation of the conserved proline catabolic gene alh-6 (88% identity to ALDH4A1 in humans) leads to premature aging and impaired muscle mitochondrial function (Pang and Curran, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pang and Curran, 2014

claim: Proline catabolism functions in a two-step reaction, beginning with the conversion of proline to 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate (P5C) which is catalyzed by proline dehydrogenase, PRDH-1.
source: Proline catabolism functions in a two-step reaction, beginning with the conversion of proline to 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate (P5C) which is catalyzed by proline dehydrogenase, PRDH-1; subsequently, P5C dehydrogenase, ALH-6, catalyzes the conversion of P5C to glutamate.
evidence: Describes established biochemical pathway

claim: P5C dehydrogenase, ALH-6, catalyzes the conversion of P5C to glutamate.
source: Proline catabolism functions in a two-step reaction, beginning with the conversion of proline to 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate (P5C) which is catalyzed by proline dehydrogenase, PRDH-1; subsequently, P5C dehydrogenase, ALH-6, catalyzes the conversion of P5C to glutamate.
evidence: Describes established biochemical pathway

claim: alh-6 expression is observed in body wall muscle, pharyngeal muscle, and neurons.
source: alh-6 expression is observed in body wall muscle, pharyngeal muscle, and neurons (Pang and Curran, 2014), and when alh-6 is mutated, the activation of gst-4p::gfp oxidative stress reporter is predominantly observed in the body wall muscle tissue and only in postreproductive adults (Tang and Pang, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pang and Curran, 2014

claim: When alh-6 is mutated, the activation of gst-4p::gfp oxidative stress reporter is predominantly observed in the body wall muscle tissue and only in postreproductive adults.
source: alh-6 expression is observed in body wall muscle, pharyngeal muscle, and neurons (Pang and Curran, 2014), and when alh-6 is mutated, the activation of gst-4p::gfp oxidative stress reporter is predominantly observed in the body wall muscle tissue and only in postreproductive adults (Tang and Pang, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tang and Pang, 2016

claim: alh-6 mutants have increased levels of P5C.
source: alh-6 mutants have increased levels of P5C; the accumulation of this toxic metabolic intermediate leads to an increase in reactive oxygen species, including H2O2 (Pang and Curran, 2014), which then activates cytoprotective responses, impairs mitochondrial activity, and drives cellular dysfunction (Pang and Curran, 2014; Pang et al., 2014; Yen et al., 2020; Yen and Curran, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pang and Curran, 2014

claim: The accumulation of P5C leads to an increase in reactive oxygen species, including H2O2.

evidence: Supported by citation to Pang and Curran, 2014

claim: Increased reactive oxygen species activates cytoprotective responses, impairs mitochondrial activity, and drives cellular dysfunction.

evidence: Supported by citations to Ke et al., 2021; Song et al., 2020; Teumer et al., 2019

source: The recent expansion of the HRS data to include genotyping of participants has enabled scans to test associations between normal aging phenotypes and variation across genes (Liu et al., 2019).

claim: The study exploits the facile genetic tractability of C. elegans with the rich genetic and phenotypic data available in the HRS to reveal genetic variation in alh-6/ALDH4A1 as a predictive indicator of muscle-related functionality in later life.
source: In this study, we exploit the facile genetic tractability of C. elegans with the rich genetic and phenotypic data available in the HRS to reveal genetic variation in alh-6/ALDH4A1 as a predictive indicator of muscle-related functionality in later life.
evidence: Statement of the study's approach and findings

claim: The strong induction of oxidative stress reporter activity in the musculature was linked to mutation of the mitochondrial P5C dehydrogenase gene.
source: While the strong induction of oxidative stress reporter activity in the musculature was linked to mutation of the mitochondrial P5C dehydrogenase gene, and not observed in other genetic mutants (Pang et al., 2014; Yen et al., 2020; Yen and Curran, 2021; Lo et al., 2017; Spatola et al., 2019; Lynn et al., 2015; Nhan et al., 2019), the breadth of genetic mutations that could induce stress responses in muscle was unknown.
evidence: Supported by citations to Pang et al., 2014; Yen et al., 2020; Yen and Curran, 2021; Lo et al., 2017; Spatola et al., 2019; Lynn et al., 2015; Nhan et al., 2019

claim: The breadth of genetic mutations that could induce stress responses in muscle was unknown.
source: While the strong induction of oxidative stress reporter activity in the musculature was linked to mutation of the mitochondrial P5C dehydrogenase gene, and not observed in other genetic mutants (Pang et al., 2014; Yen et al., 2020; Yen and Curran, 2021; Lo et al., 2017; Spatola et al., 2019; Lynn et al., 2015; Nhan et al., 2019), the breadth of genetic mutations that could induce stress responses in muscle was unknown.
evidence: Statement of knowledge gap prior to this study

claim: An ethyl methanesulfonate mutagenesis screen was performed selecting for the age-dependent activation of the gst-4p::gfp reporter in the musculature.
source: In order to identify additional genetic components of this age-related muscle phenotype, we performed an ethyl methanesulfonate mutagenesis screen selecting for the same age-dependent activation of the gst-4p::gfp reporter in the musculature.
evidence: Description of experimental method used in the study

claim: The screen isolated 96 mutant animals with age-dependent activation of the gst-4p::gfp reporter restricted to the body wall musculature.
source: We screened the progeny of ~4000 mutagenized F1 animals and isolated 96 mutant animals with age-dependent activation of the gst-4p::gfp reporter restricted to the body wall musculature, which phenocopies the alh-6(lax105) mutant (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Experimental result from mutagenesis screen, with reference to Figure 1a and Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: All 96 new mutations failed to complement the alh-6(lax105) allele and are loss-of-function alleles of alh-6.
source: To rule out additional loss-of-function alleles of alh-6 we performed genetic complementation (cis–trans) testing with our established alh-6(lax105) allele; surprisingly, all 96 new mutations failed to complement and as such were all loss-of-function alleles of alh-6.
evidence: Result from genetic complementation testing

claim: After sequencing approximately half of the mutants, several distinct molecular lesions in alh-6 were repeatedly and independently isolated.
source: After sequencing approximately half of the mutants, we noted the repeated independent isolation of several distinct molecular lesions in alh-6: E78Stop (lax903, lax918, lax930), E447K (lax916, lax920, lax929, lax934), G527R (lax914, lax932, lax933, lax947), etc. (Figure 1b).
evidence: Sequencing results with reference to Figure 1b

claim: The lack of diversity in genes uncovered and the independent isolation of identical alleles multiple times from this unbiased screen strongly suggest genetic saturation and specificity of this response to animals with defective mitochondrial proline catabolism.
source: The lack of diversity in genes uncovered and the independent isolation of identical alleles multiple times from this unbiased screen strongly suggest genetic saturation and specificity of this response to animals with defective mitochondrial proline catabolism.
evidence: Inference drawn from the pattern of mutations isolated in the screen

claim: Several mutations mapped to discrete regions of the linear ALH-6 polypeptide, including G152/K153, G199/E201/G202, and E418/G419, which may define critical domains in the folded protein.
source: In addition, several mutations mapped to discreet regions of the linear ALH-6 polypeptide, including G152/K153, G199/E201/G202, and E418/G419, which may define critical domains in the folded protein.
evidence: Observation from mutation mapping with speculative interpretation

claim: Each mutant was phenotypically identical to lax105 in the activation of the gst-4p::gfp stress reporter in the bodywall muscle at day 3 of adulthood.
source: Imaging at day 3 of adulthood revealed that each mutant was phenotypically identical to lax105 in the activation of the gst-4p::gfp stress reporter in the bodywall muscle (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), but with varying intensity (Figure 1c).
evidence: Imaging results with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 1c

claim: The mutants showed varying intensity of gst-4p::gfp stress reporter activation.
source: Imaging at day 3 of adulthood revealed that each mutant was phenotypically identical to lax105 in the activation of the gst-4p::gfp stress reporter in the bodywall muscle (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), but with varying intensity (Figure 1c).
evidence: Quantitative data shown in Figure 1c

claim: Most missense mutations were predicted to maintain the overall structure (no structural damage), which suggests the associated phenotypes derive from a range of reduction of function mutations.
source: Most missense mutations were predicted to maintain the overall structure (no structural damage), which suggests the associated phenotypes derive from a range of reduction of function mutations.
evidence: Inference from structural prediction modeling

claim: The degree of mitochondrial dysfunction can influence both beneficial and detrimental physiological outcomes.
source: Since the degree of mitochondrial dysfunction can influence both beneficial and detrimental physiological outcomes (Wang and Hekimi, 2015; Shields et al., 2021), this collection of mutants provides a model to understand the complex role mitochondria play in organismal health over the lifespan.
evidence: Supported by citations to Wang and Hekimi, 2015; Shields et al., 2021

claim: This collection of mutants provides a model to understand the complex role mitochondria play in organismal health over the lifespan.
source: Since the degree of mitochondrial dysfunction can influence both beneficial and detrimental physiological outcomes (Wang and Hekimi, 2015; Shields et al., 2021), this collection of mutants provides a model to understand the complex role mitochondria play in organismal health over the lifespan.
evidence: Inference about the utility of the mutant collection

claim: The age-dependent and muscle activation of the gst-4p::gfp is driven specifically by mutations in mitochondrial alh-6.
source: Taken together, these data reveal that the age-dependent and muscle activation of the gst-4p::gfp is driven specifically by mutations in mitochondrial alh-6.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the genetic screen and complementation data

claim: ALDH4A1 genetic variants would associate with phenotypes indexing normative, longitudinal changes in human aging-related functionality, specifically those that involve usage of different muscle groups.
source: Based on the striking specificity of the muscle-restricted and age-dependent activation of the gst-4p::gfp stress reporter in C. elegans harboring mutations in alh-6 (Pang and Curran, 2014; Yen et al., 2020), combined with the high degree of conservation in mitochondrial metabolism pathways across metazoans (Pang et al., 2014), we reasoned that ALDH4A1 genetic variants would associate with phenotypes indexing normative, longitudinal changes in human aging-related functionality, specifically those that involve usage of different muscle groups.
evidence: Hypothesis based on C. elegans data and evolutionary conservation, supported by citations

claim: Gene-wide association scanning (GeneWAS) was performed in the US HRS.
source: To test this hypothesis, we performed gene-wide association scanning (GeneWAS) adjusting for relevant covariates and indicators of population stratification in the US HRS; a nationally representative longitudinal study of >36,000 adults over age 50 in the United States (Sonnega et al., 2014; Weir, 2013).
evidence: Description of experimental approach with citations

claim: HRS is a nationally representative longitudinal study of >36,000 adults over age 50 in the United States.
source: To test this hypothesis, we performed gene-wide association scanning (GeneWAS) adjusting for relevant covariates and indicators of population stratification in the US HRS; a nationally representative longitudinal study of >36,000 adults over age 50 in the United States (Sonnega et al., 2014; Weir, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Sonnega et al., 2014; Weir, 2013

claim: HRS collects biological and genetic samples on subsets of participants and assesses physical and psychosocial measures of all study participants in older adulthood, including multiple measures of muscle-related functionality.
source: HRS collects biological and genetic samples on subsets of participants and assesses physical and psychosocial measures of all study participants in older adulthood, including multiple measures of muscle-related functionality (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: Description of HRS data collection with reference to Figure 2—source data 1

claim: There were 70 single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers within the ALDH4A1 region on the Illumina Omni array representing 273 human SNPs in the gene.
source: There were 70 single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers within the ALDH4A1 region that are on the Illumina Omni array representing 273 human SNPs in the gene.
evidence: Description of genetic data available for analysis

claim: Two associations between variants within ALDH4A1 and two phenotypes were detected and surpassed the respective empirical p value thresholds, determined by permutation testing.
source: Overall, two associations between variants within ALDH4A1 and two phenotypes were detected and surpassed the respective empirical p value thresholds, determined by permutation testing (Tables 1 and 2).
evidence: Statistical results from GeneWAS with reference to Tables 1 and 2

claim: These demonstrate a pattern of association between ALDH4A1 variation and two independent phenotypes.
source: These demonstrate a pattern of association between ALDH4A1 variation and two independent phenotypes (Table 1).
evidence: Conclusion from statistical analysis with reference to Table 1

claim: This GeneWAS was unable to directly identify a causal variant.
source: Because each of the SNPs within the ALDH4A1 region represents a tag, or marker SNP for human variation within the locus, this GeneWAS was unable to directly identify a causal variant; however, the indexing of variations within the same gene suggests conserved associations within this aging human cohort.
evidence: Limitation of the study design acknowledged by authors

claim: The indexing of variations within the same gene suggests conserved associations within this aging human cohort.
source: Because each of the SNPs within the ALDH4A1 region represents a tag, or marker SNP for human variation within the locus, this GeneWAS was unable to directly identify a causal variant; however, the indexing of variations within the same gene suggests conserved associations within this aging human cohort.

claim: rs77608580 was significantly associated with change in gait speed over time.
source: rs77608580 was significantly associated with change in gait speed over time (Figure 2a).
evidence: Statistical result with reference to Figure 2a

claim: With each additional A allele of rs77608580, there was an average increase in gait speed of 0.052 m per second per year compared to other same aged individuals without the allele (p value = 0.0025).
source: Specifically, with each additional A allele, there was an average increase in gait speed of 0.052 m per second per year compared to other same aged individuals without the allele (p value = 0.0025, surpassing the empirical p value threshold of 0.006).
evidence: Statistical result from regression analysis

claim: The association between rs77608580 and gait speed was assessed among N = 3319 older individuals with a mean age of 73.0 years (SD = 5.9) and mean gait speed of 0.80 m per second (SD = 0.25).
source: This was assessed among N = 3319 older individuals with a mean age of 73.0 years (standard deviation [SD] = 5.9) and mean gait speed of 0.80 m per second (SD = 0.25), or 2.6 ft/s (Figure 3a).
evidence: Descriptive statistics of the study sample with reference to Figure 3a

claim: rs28665699 was significantly associated with an increase in grip strength over time.
source: Measures of muscle health, such as grip strength, are effective biomarkers of overall health in older populations (Carson, 2018; McGrath et al., 2020). rs28665699 was significantly associated with an increase in grip strength over time (Figure 2b); with each additional A allele, there was an average increase in grip strength by 0.045 kg weight per year while holding all other characteristics constant (age, sex, and use of the dominant hand for gripping; p value = 0.0009, surpassing the empirical p value threshold of 0.0019).
evidence: Statistical result with reference to Figure 2b

claim: With each additional A allele of rs28665699, there was an average increase in grip strength by 0.045 kg weight per year (p value = 0.0009).
source: rs28665699 was significantly associated with an increase in grip strength over time (Figure 2b); with each additional A allele, there was an average increase in grip strength by 0.045 kg weight per year while holding all other characteristics constant (age, sex, and use of the dominant hand for gripping; p value = 0.0009, surpassing the empirical p value threshold of 0.0019).
evidence: Statistical result from regression analysis

claim: The association between rs28665699 and grip strength was assessed among N = 5228 older individuals with a mean age of 68.9 years (SD = 10.4), mean grip strength of 30.21 kg (SD = 11.1), and average level of decline in grip strength at 2.31 kg per year (SD = 5.37).
source: This was assessed among N = 5228 older individuals with a mean age of 68.9 years (SD = 10.4), mean grip strength of 30.21 kg (SD = 11.1), and average level of decline in grip strength at 2.31 kg per year (SD = 5.37).
evidence: Descriptive statistics of the study sample

claim: Over a 10-year period, those with one or two effect alleles of rs28665699 would have stronger grip by 0.5 and 1.0 kg compared to those without an effect allele, respectively.
source: If calculated as change over a 10-year period, those with one or two effect alleles would have stronger grip by 0.5 and 1.0 kg compared to those without an effect allele, respectively. The allele therefore is associated with a slower rate of decline in grip strength over a decade of age (Figure 3b).
evidence: Calculation based on regression results with reference to Figure 3b

claim: The allele rs28665699 is associated with a slower rate of decline in grip strength over a decade of age.
source: If calculated as change over a 10-year period, those with one or two effect alleles would have stronger grip by 0.5 and 1.0 kg compared to those without an effect allele, respectively. The allele therefore is associated with a slower rate of decline in grip strength over a decade of age (Figure 3b).
evidence: Inference from statistical results with reference to Figure 3b

source: These effects are examples where variation in the gene contributing to phenotypes that represent different age-related change in functionality; overall we find there are small effects associated with each phenotype, but there are possible pleiotropic effects, and environmental or behavioral factors contributing.

claim: The panel of alh-6 mutants displayed differences in developmental and adult swimming performance.
source: Intriguingly, the effect of the canonical alh-6(lax105) mutation on swimming was less pronounced than that observed for crawling speed and our panel of alh-6 mutants displayed differences in developmental and adult swimming performance.

source: Taken together these data support the age-specific acceleration of muscle decline in mitochondrial proline catabolism mutants, which is conserved from nematodes to humans.
